officialTitle: Tamoxifen in treatment of intraductal breast cancer: National Surgical Adjuvant Breast and Bowel Project B-24 randomised controlled trial
setting: Adjuvant therapy after lumpectomy and radiotherapy for DCIS

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: 1804 women with DCIS, including those whose resected sample margins were involved with tumour, were randomly assigned lumpectomy, radiation therapy (50 Gy), and placebo (n=902), or lumpectomy, radiation therapy, and tamoxifen (20 mg daily for 5 years, n=902).
primaryEndpoints: Invasive and non-invasive ipsilateral and contralateral breast cancer events
design.notes: Women with involved margins were eligible; ER status was not an entry criterion in the abstract.

clinicalQuestion: After lumpectomy and radiotherapy for DCIS, does adding tamoxifen reduce subsequent breast cancer events?

pico.population: Women with DCIS treated with lumpectomy and radiotherapy, including those with involved margins
pico.outcomes: Ipsilateral and contralateral invasive and non-invasive breast cancer events

arms.label: Lumpectomy + RT + tamoxifen
arms.dosing: Tamoxifen 20 mg daily for 5 years; radiotherapy 50 Gy
arms.doseSourceQuote: 1804 women with DCIS, including those whose resected sample margins were involved with tumour, were randomly assigned lumpectomy, radiation therapy (50 Gy), and placebo (n=902), or lumpectomy, radiation therapy, and tamoxifen (20 mg daily for 5 years, n=902).

publications.title: Tamoxifen in treatment of intraductal breast cancer: National Surgical Adjuvant Breast and Bowel Project B-24 randomised controlled trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Women in the tamoxifen group had fewer breast-cancer events at 5 years than did those on placebo (8.2 vs 13.4%, p=0.0009).

outcomes.endpointLabel: Cumulative incidence of invasive breast cancer events at 5 years
outcomes.sourceQuote: The cumulative incidence of all invasive breast-cancer events in the tamoxifen group was 4.1% at 5 years: 2.1% in the ipsilateral breast, 1.8% in the contralateral breast, and 0.2% at regional or distant sites.

strengths: Included women with involved margins and comedonecrosis
limitations: ER status not required for entry, so benefit by receptor status cannot be judged from the abstract
No survival endpoint reported in the abstract

clinicalImplications.text: Supports considering adjuvant tamoxifen after breast-conserving surgery and radiotherapy for DCIS to reduce ipsilateral and contralateral breast cancer events.

tumourBoardPearl.text: In DCIS the endocrine benefit is risk reduction of new breast events, both ipsilateral and contralateral — frame the discussion around prevention rather than survival.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 10376613. No registry number is printed in the abstract.
